name: collective
description: The Collective operator safety floor for Claude Code. What it sends: While the collective MCP server is connected, Claude Code's mcp_tool PreToolUse hook sends the full text of every proposed Bash command, inline secrets included, to that server's rules engine (collective_validate_command). That is the plugin's one automatic network call; it runs in every repo, including for commands that are then blocked or declined. The commit check, only in a Collective-governed repo: After a git commit whose message carries an ac:<id> tag, it asks the agent to call collective_record_commit, which sends that commit's SHA, subject and tags to the collective server while it is connected, over the agent's own authenticated MCP session. It reads the new commit's SHA and message (git) and the repo's CLAUDE.md, to tell whether the repo is Collective-governed. The artifact check, in any repo: After a claude.ai Artifact publish, it asks the agent to send the artifact's full text, URL and title (and the signed-in account if known) to the collective server while that server is connected; when it is not connected, the agent skips it. It reads the published local file for its size, hash and title. The c-* skills, when run, have the agent send plans, specs, diffs and findings to the collective server and use git, gh, npm and deploy tools under your permissions. Local state: the commit check keeps the commit SHAs it has asked about in nudged-commits, and the artifact check keeps artifact URLs and content hashes in mirrored-artifacts, both under $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, or $HOME/.collective when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA is unset. Inside: a catastrophic-command denylist (recursive root deletion, DROP DATABASE, fork bombs, force-push to protected branches, etc.) whose every denial says how to proceed when the matched pattern was only text the command carried, a protected-file guard on platform-safety files, a UserPromptSubmit claim-gate contract, and the c-* workflow skills. The hook scripts run locally and read no credentials.
